newsitem.title: USA: Flagstar Cos files Chapter 11 plan.
newsitem.headline: Flagstar Cos files Chapter 11 plan.

text.p: Flagstar Cos Inc said on Friday that it filed a voluntary Chapter 11 plan with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in South Carolina.
The restaurant company said in a news release that its plan already has been approved by its creditors.
Flagstar said it enters the Chapter 11 proceeding with an agreement for a $200 million debtor-in-possession revolving credit facility from Chase Manhattan Corp.

The company also said it had a written commitment from Chase for a $200 million senior secured revolving credit facility that would finance the debtor-in-possession facility upon Flagstar's emergence from Chapter 11.

Flagstar said the proceeding involved only itself and its Flagstar Corp and Flagstar Holdings Inc units. The subsidiaries that operate the company's 3,200 restaurants -- including such brands as Carrow's, Coco's, Denny's, El Pollo Loco and Quincy's Family Steakhouse -- will not be affected, the parent company said.
Flagstar said final approval of the plan would complete a restructuring process that would allow it to shed $1.1 billion in debt and preferred stock.

"We enter this process with the enthusiastic support of all but our smallest class of debtholders, sufficient liquidity from our operations and the bank financing we have arranged," Flagstar Chairman/Chief Executive James Adamson said in the news release.
